title: Exactness and finiteness in the Zariski-small-etale module comparison
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. For a quasi-coherent Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-module $F$ [pqf-def-coherent], let $A_T(F)=F_{\mathrm{et}}$ be its associated sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], with $A_T(F)(u:U\to T)=\Gamma(U,u^*F)$ on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Regard the functor $A_T$ of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] as taking values in all sheaves of $\mathcal O_{T,\mathrm{et}}$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with quasi-coherent essential image [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. This functor is exact: it takes every short exact sequence of quasi-coherent Zariski modules to a short exact sequence in the ambient small-etale module category. Moreover $F$ is of finite type, respectively of finite presentation, if and only if $A_T(F)$ is of finite type, respectively of finite presentation. On either site these properties mean locally admitting an epimorphism $\mathcal O^{\oplus n}\twoheadrightarrow F$, respectively an exact sequence $\mathcal O^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O^{\oplus n}\to F\to0$, with $m,n<\infty$; locally means Zariski locally on the Zariski site and etale locally on the small etale site. No Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 06VE, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-limits, part (5), only the small etale site; Tag 05VG, lemma-equivalence-quasi-coherent-properties, finite type and finite presentation.

proof.text: The specified canonical extension has the context adjunction to restriction. Restriction is additive sectionwise; the adjunction makes extension additive and a left adjoint, hence it preserves cokernels and epimorphisms.

For a monomorphism between quasi-coherent modules, every small-etale test map is flat, so tensor pullback preserves that monomorphism. Evaluation on global sections preserves monomorphisms. The tensor-section comparison and its naturality conjugate the components of the extended map to these injective section maps. Thus every component is mono, and the faithful forgetful functors from module sheaves to additive sheaves to presheaves reflect monomorphisms. This proves preservation of monomorphisms without constructing quasi-coherent kernels.

Given an ambient short exact sequence with quasi-coherent terms, right exactness sends its cokernel presentation to an exact sequence with epi last map. Step 2 makes the first map mono. Functoriality and preservation of zero supply the zero composite, so the mapped short complex is short exact.

Apply the finiteness-preservation lemma for the two forward implications. For either reverse implication, local recovery supplies an etale fpqc covering whose Zariski pullbacks have the appropriate finiteness property. Finite type descends by isFiniteType_of_fpqc_tensorPullback. For finite presentation pass from the precoverage to its generated covering sieve and apply fpqc finite-presentation descent to the canonical descent datum of F with its identity comparison isomorphism.

lean.statement: theorem scheme_etale_module_exact_finiteness_comparison (T : Scheme.{u}) : (∀ (S : ShortComplex T.Modules), S.X₁.IsQuasicoherent → S.X₂.IsQuasicoherent → S.X₃.IsQuasicoherent → S.ShortExact → ∃ h : (schemeEtaleModuleComparison T).map S.f ≫ (schemeEtaleModuleComparison T).map S.g = 0, (ShortComplex.mk ((schemeEtaleModuleComparison T).map S.f) ((schemeEtaleModuleComparison T).map S.g) h).ShortExact) ∧ (∀ (F : T.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent], (F.IsFiniteType ↔ ((schemeEtaleModuleComparison T).obj F).IsFiniteType) ∧ (F.IsFinitePresentation ↔ ((schemeEtaleModuleComparison T).obj F).IsFinitePresentation))
lean.note: The helper is a transparent abbreviation of the recorded canonical tensor extension. Classical.choose extracts only the proof-only context guaranteed by the comparison theorem; it selects no arbitrary module, map or functor. Short exactness is stated for the explicitly mapped arrows in the full SmallEtaleModules category; the existential zero-composition proof constructs that short complex without assuming a separate preservation-of-zero instance.
